Technical Article · Genetic Engineering PROPOSED

Deterministic Grounding for Agent Software Engineering

How to anchor context, restrict actions and validate changes without confusing a green result with global correction.

An agent can produce syntactically correct code, pass available tests and violate the architecture, scope, privacy or current status of the repository.

Agent Preferences (A t)

Prompt: "Add PDF Export Route"
Recovered context: RAG Index (Commit C1)
Hypothesis: PDF-kit Dep v1.2 present
Plan: Modify src/api/export.js and package. json

Repository Observable Status (S t)

Snapshot: Committee C2 (HEAD)
Lockfile: pdf-kit removed in C2
Policy: src/api/ restricted by ADR-014
Diff Real: Change in C1 generates conflict in C2

Agent–Repository Gap: G t = Premes(A t) − Predicates verified(S t)

"Right code in isolation can still be a wrong change."

Scene 01 · The Agent–Repository Gap

A t, S t, D, G t and 5 System States

To prevent the action of the agent from being guided by obsolete assumptions or context illusions, it is necessary to rigidly separate the authority of each state:

Current State
Repository / Runtime
OBSERVED
Desired State (D)
Specification / Requirements
PROPOSED
Historical State
Memory / RAG / Commits
INFERENCE
Policy State
Action Gateway / Rules
DOCUMENTED
Evidence State
Oracles / Validation
STABLISHED

Current State

Authority: Repository / Runtime (what is observed now)

Which allows you to say:

  • Confirm commit SHA, file tree, lockfile and dependencies installed in snapshot.
  • Check the state of uncommitted changes and the current build.

Which does NOT allow to state:

  • Affirm human intentions or future requirements.
  • Ensure that the ideal architecture is being respected without external verification.
· Counterexample: Stale Context and Architecture Violation

Scene: Agent recovers context index built on commit C1. The repository has advanced to C2, where a new architectural rule prohibits direct bank calls in the controller.

Success Appearance: The code generated is syntactically correct, compiles and passes the isolated unit tests.

Unobserved property: RAG alignment with current SHA (C2) and the new layer coupling rule.

Lesson: Recovered text consistency is not current from the repository.

Scene 03 · Contracts & Requirements PROPOSED

From Human Intention to Verifiable Contract

Prompt is not a contract. Human intent must pass through a transformation line with formal criteria and explicit negative properties.

Human Need → Intent → Desired State (D) → Minimum Requirement → Contract (4 Levels) → Oracle → Evidence

Level 1 · Interface

Types, schemas, signatures of methods and message formats.

Level 2 · Behavior

Preconditions, post-conditions, invariants and side effects.

Level 3 · Architecture

Layers, module borders, permitted dependencies and isolation.

Level 4 · Semantics

Ownership of data, privacy, retention and regulatory impacts.

· Counterexample: Photo Service and Hidden Privacy

Scene: The agent implements a photo upload service. All API tests (Level 1 and 2) return PASS.

Success Appearance: The API sends and stores photos with excellent response time.

Unobserved property: The implementation records EXIF with location on open logs and shares metadata with third parties without consent (Level Violation 4).

Lesson: The main path of PASS API remains green, but a side track remains unvalid by absence of oracle.

Scene 04 · Structural Analysis PROPOSED

Software as Partial Structure

Static analysis and code graphs (AST/CST, symbols and typed relationships) provide structural grounding, but have inherent observability boundaries. No static analysis captures runtime completely.

Boundary Marker: The graph represents only statically extractable predicates. Calls via reflection, eval, dynamic plugins or code generation in runtime end in POSSIBLE or UNKNOWN, and should never be treated as nonexistent.

Scene 05 · Governance of Action DOCUMENTED

Autonomy is not Authority & Action Gateway

Advanced models can propose complex plans autonomously. However, the authority to apply changes to the repository, shoot deploys or invoke privileged tools belongs exclusively to the Action Gateway.

Low Autonomy · Low Authority

Rigid automation, local scripts and routine reading tasks.

Low Autonomy · High Authority

Deploy Scripts with high radius blast without flexible verification.

High Autonomy · Low Authority (Recommended Zone)

Agent investigates, plans and proposes changes; execution is strictly mediated and limited to sandbox.

High Autonomy · High Authority (High Risk Zone)

Agent decides and executes directly in production. Dangerous merger of decision and execution.

Action Gateway · The 12 Check Steps

01. Receive unreliable proposal
02. Normalize tool and version
03. Validate input schema
04. Solve canonical resources
05. Identify main and environment
06. Check scope and allowlist
07. Calculate blast radius / fan-out
08. Consult Policy-as-Code
09. Check Linked Approval
10. Revalidate pre-effect snapshot
11. Run with Minimum Privilege
12. Register evidence / provenance

Diff Lens · Action Scope Interception

[Proposed by Agent] Modify src/api/export.js and infra/deploy. yaml
[Authorized Scope] Allowlist: src/api/** only
[Action interrupted by Gateway] Attempted change outside the scope in infra/deploy.yaml. No effect applied.
· Counterexample: Secondary Call with High Authority

Scene: An innocent reading tool (release status) is invoked. A ticket induces the agent to internally call a second tool (sync environment) with written permission.

Success Appearance: The first call passes the initial reading check.

Unobserved property: The second call appears as a new entity on the pipeline and requires independent mediation by Action Gateway.

Lesson: Valid schema and approval of the primary call do not authorize privileged secondary chains.

Scene 06 · Epistemological Force STABLISHED

The Green Result is Less than It Seems

A Green Test (PASS) proves only that the tested property was satisfied under the observed execution envelope. It doesn't prove global correction or absence of collateral.

Filter by Verdict: Displaying 10 of 10 oracles (0 hidden)
Oracle / Validator Verdict What the PASS establishes WHAT DOES NOT ESTABLISH ALONE
01. Parser (Syntax) PASS Analysable entry as grammar of language. Correct typing, semantics or functioning.
02. Type Checker PASS Types satisfy the static type system rules. Behavior in runtime or absence of logical bugs.
03. Static Analysis / Linter PASS Linter rule and abstract patterns satisfied. Completeness and absence of functional regressions.
04. Unit Test PASS Specific case executed passed under defined inputs. Unwritten border cases or omitted requirements.
05. Integration Test PASS Components interacted successfully in the tested scenario. Behavior under high competition or in prod.
06. Security Scanner PASS No known vulnerability signatures found. Absence of unprecedented business logic failures.
07. Runtime Monitor UNKNOWN Normal metrics during the captured window. Behavior in windows not observed or peak.
08. Model Checker FAIL Formal model satisfies invariant properties. Absolute loyalty from model to concrete code.
09. Formal Checker CONFLICK Math evidence of correspondence with spec. Correction of the original human intention of the spec.
10. Human Review PASS Human evaluator approved the change according to his judgment. Math guarantee against omission or revision failure.
· Counterexample: Disabled and False Green Aggregate Test

Scene: The test test rejects negative amount() failure after a change. To converge, the test is marked with skip.

Success Appearance: The test suite in the IC is 100% green (0 apparent failures).

Unobserved property: The decrease in coverage of the expected test inventory. The skip hides the gap instead of solving it.

Lesson: Less failed testing doesn't mean more correct software — it just means less observation.

Scene 08 · Decision & Closing PROPOSED

Reconciliation, MVA & Baseline Comparer

Reconciliation compares the desired state (D), current state (S t), evidence obtained and policy rules to issue one of the 7 possible decisions.

01. Desired State (D)

Invariants and declared acceptance requirements.

02. Current State

Diff from the post-action agent repository.

03. Evidence State

Evidence Record with verdicts and limits.

04. Policy State

Allowlist of scope and approval of action.

At 7. Reconciliation Process Outputs

1. Accept Change: Satisfactory evidence and within the policy.
2. Block Change: Scope violation or oracle failure.
3. Request Human Review: High impact or uncertainty detected.
4. Start New Cycle: Reschedule plan for the agent.
5. Fix Oracle: Test flaky or incorrect oracle.
6. Change Spec: Human explicit decision to change requirement.
7. Term Exception: Temporary release accompanied.

Start with an MVA (Minimum Viable Architecture)

Implement a low-risk pipeline following the 7 operational action checklist:

  1. Choose a low impact delimited task.
  2. Fix Snapshot Capsule (SHA, tree digest and lockfile).
  3. State allowlist and file denylist on Action Gateway.
  4. Turn at least one requirement into independent contract and oracle.
  5. Run the agent in a sandbox without implied authority.
  6. Register explicitly verdicts PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN and CONFLICK at Evidence Record.
  7. Compare the results with a baseline without grounding.
Set First Envelope

In short

What is Deterministic Grounding

A development agent can produce syntactically correct code, pass isolated tests and still violate the architecture, authorized scope or actual status of the repository. Deterministic Grounding establishes explicit state anchoring, authority limitation by Action Gateway and validation with auditable oracles.

  • Agent–Repository Gap (G t) — the difference between what the agent believes (A t) and what was observed in the repository (S t).
  • Snapshot Capsule — immutable envelope that seals commit, tree, lockfile and environment before action.
  • Action Gateway — 12-step barrier preventing execution outside the scope (Diff Lens and allowlist).
  • Evidence Record — registration with bounded verdicts (PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN, CONFLICT) and observation borders.

Integrates the journey of Trust Engineering and AI Agent Engineering.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Agent–Repository Gap?

It is the difference between the premises that guide the action of the agent in the context A t and verifiable predicates about the observable state S t in the repository.

Why does a green test result (PASS) not guarantee global correction?

Because an oracle tests only one specific property under a restricted execution envelope. He does not observe collaterals out of its scope, privacy leaks or unmapped architectural violations in the test.

What is Snapshot Capsule?

It is the immutable envelope containing commit SHA, branch, tree digest, lockfile, toolchain, execution environment and a unique digest that ensures that the agent context corresponds exactly to the repository state.

What's the difference between Autonomy and Authority?

Autonomy is the ability of the model to plan and chain actions flexibly; Authority is the effective permission to produce effects on the repository, which must be restricted and mediated by Action Gateway.
